# Week 5 Game Plan: Pittsburgh

**Head coach:** Alex Stone  
**Game:** Pittsburgh at Jacksonville, Sunday, October 5, 2014, 1 p.m. ET, EverBank Field  
**Briefing used:** September 28, 2014  
**Baseline:** Carry Week 4

## 1. What I want this game to look like

**The matchup I am attacking:** Useful tight-end routes against Pittsburgh's linebackers and safeties, with Kelce in the receiving Y job on the crossing and mesh calls and protection that releases the intended receiver.  
**What I must not give them:** Bell and Blount running through an automatic dime; six defensive backs only against true passing situations, with the front still able to fit the run.  
**What would make me change course:** A shift or pressure answer that is not clean, or a Kelce combination that is not ready, sends us back to the established Lewis assignments.

## 2. Game-day availability and personnel

**Inactives:** Jordan Poyer (independent medical hold), Malcolm Butler, Jonathan Grimes, Corey Linsley, Kasim Edebali, Taylor Gabriel, Gator Hoskins  
**Depth/role changes:** No change  
**If Posluszny, Stanford or Phillips cannot dress:** The prepared linebacker and kicking-game contingencies of the week; reissue after the examination.  
**Special coverage and substitution consequences:** Todd Davis dresses in Hoskins's place for linebacker and coverage-unit depth.

## 3. Offense: what we are calling and why

**Caller:** Alex Stone  
**Base personnel and roles:** Jones-Drew is the normal-down back and Anderson enters for an identified relief series; Lewis is the established Y, Kelce TE2 with the receiving emphasis; Nicks is X relief only on prepared series while Adams rests.  
**The first things I want to learn:** Who handles both tight ends after the defense has seen the run, the safety fit on Power, and whether the backside edge chases the Outside Zone.  
**Opening approach:** Show the twelve-personnel run first, then the tight-end throws; a numbered call is an eligible option, never a command to ignore down, distance or coverage.  
**Opening calls, in order:** 12 Ace, Power Right; 12 SHIFT Empty, Stick; 12 Trey, Y-Cross, SOLID; 11 Bunch, Mesh, HALF; 12 Wing, Outside Zone Left; 12 Wing, Boot Flood Right; 12 Ace, Power Right; 12 SHIFT Empty, Stick; 12 Ace, Counter Right; 11 Doubles, Drive, HALF; 12 Trey, Y-Cross, SOLID; 11 Doubles, Stick, SCAT; 11 Doubles, RB Slow Screen; 12 Ace, Power Left; 11 Bunch, Mesh, HALF; 12 Ace, Flea Flicker, MAX; 12 Wing, TE Delay; 11 SHIFT Empty, Spacing, SCAT; 11 Doubles, Inside Zone Right; 12 Wing, Outside Zone Left; 12 Wing, Boot Flood Right; 12 Trey, Y-Cross, SOLID; 11 Trips, Inside Zone + Bubble; 12 Ace, Power Pass / Post-Cross, MAX; 12 Ace, Counter Right; 12 SHIFT Empty, Stick; 11 Trey, Dagger, HALF; 12 Ace, Power Right; 11 Bunch, Mesh, HALF; 12 Trey, Y-Cross, SOLID

### Primary calls

| Call / concept as named in the active book | When I want it | Football reason and key read | Protection, personnel or stop condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 Trey, Y-Cross, SOLID (Kelce receiving Y) | normal downs, second and long, third and long, high red zone, four-minute | Kelce in the primary crossing job, the cross read against linebacker and safety leverage | Coverage still decides the throw; the Lewis combination if the Kelce job is not ready |
| 11 Bunch, Mesh, HALF (Kelce receiving Y) | normal downs, second and long, third and short, third and medium, high red zone, low red zone, two-point tries, two-minute, PRESS sequence | The crossers against man and the taught sit against zone | No forced tight-end throw |
| 12 Wing, Boot Flood Right | high red zone, low red zone, two-point tries, four-minute, sudden change | The tight ends' intermediate and flat distribution under the edge rule | Only after a confirmed backside chase |
| 11 Doubles, Drive, HALF (Nicks X relief) | second and long, third and medium, third and long, two-minute, PRESS sequence | The shallow and dig against underneath leverage | Shortened if protection cannot hold the intermediate route |
| 11 Doubles, Stick, SCAT (Kelce receiving Y, Nicks X relief) | normal downs, third and medium, backed up, two-minute, PRESS sequence | The extra rusher identified and the immediate answer | Backed up only with a known pressure answer |
| 11 Doubles, RB Slow Screen | second and long, third and long, two-minute, PRESS sequence | Only against a credible rush | Never because it is next on the list |
| 11 SHIFT Empty, Spacing, SCAT | two-minute, PRESS sequence | The back-to-empty communication and the underneath distribution | Skipped if the formation is not clean |
| 11 Doubles, Inside Zone Right | backed up | Jones-Drew against a favorable structure | No run into an unblocked defender |
| 11 Trips, Inside Zone + Bubble | third and short | The taught box and overhang count | The access is a defined answer, not an extra read |

### Situational changes from the standing / previous menu

**Third down:** Short: Power, Counter, Mesh or the Bubble count; medium: Stick, Mesh and Drive; long: the protected intermediate menu with the Dagger only behind clean protection.  
**Backed up:** Power, Inside Zone, Outside Zone and Stick with a known pressure answer; no flea flicker and no slow shot.  
**High red zone, low red zone, goal line:** Power, the Y-Cross, Mesh and the gated boot high; Mesh, Snag, Power and Counter low; Power both ways and Counter at the goal line.  
**Two-minute / hurry-up:** Stick, Spacing, Drive, Mesh and the screen; the practiced PRESS sequence only.  
**Four-minute / protect a lead:** Jones-Drew's Power, Counter and Outside Zone, with the Y-Cross and the gated boot against a loaded front.  
**Sudden change / shot opportunities:** A sound base call first; a turnover by itself does not make the Flea Flicker favorable.  
**Special plays:** 12 Ace, Flea Flicker, MAX: Keep, only after the safety response on the Power looks supports it; 12 Wing, TE Delay: Keep, only against a credible rush  
**Calls not available this week:** 12 Trey, Y-Cross, HALF (no line of the plan names it)

## 4. Defense: what we are showing and answering

**Caller:** Alex Stone  
**Base front and run fits:** Force, cutback and the plus-one fitter are the first gate on every call against Bell and Blount.  
**Coverage and rush approach:** Quarters and 6 as the weekly emphasis, four-man replacement pressure, and a situational dime.  
**Rush rule:** Four unless I call the five-man counter  
**What we need to discover early:** How their protection handles the replaced rusher, and who travels with the second tight end.

| Offensive situation / presentation | Prepared front, coverage or pressure response | Football reason | Counter / when to get out of it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Second and long | Nickel | Keep the run credible | Dime only against a true pass picture |
| Third and medium | Nickel Quarters or Cover 1 Robber, base four | Release leverage, Bell's location and the sticks | A qualified four-man Replace |
| Third and long | Dime Quarters or Cover 6, base four | Show the common threat picture | Field or Boundary Replace after the checks |
| Red zone | Quarters or Cover 1 Robber | Minimum disguise | The heavy answer near the goal line |
| Late lead | Quarters or Cover 6, base four | Four rush, seven in coverage | Replacement pressure stays conditional |
| Two-minute | Quarters or Cover 6, base four | Four rush, seven in coverage | Current personnel if tempo blocks a substitution |
| When the offense shows a pass picture | Dime | Six defensive backs for pass pictures | Back to Nickel when the run is credible |
| When Dime is on the field | Dime, base four | The base four is primary | A qualified change-up |
| If the change-up goes to the field | Dime, Replace Field | Bouye replaces Mincey and owns field contain | Out of it if contain is in doubt |
| If the change-up goes to the boundary | Dime, Replace Boundary | Prosinski replaces Branch and owns boundary contain | Out of it if contain is in doubt |
| When we show the interior mug | Dime, interior mug | A presentation, not an extra rusher | Still four rush |
| 12 personnel, credible heavy run | Under Y Quarters, base four | Start with the base four | Out of Dime |
| 11 personnel, balanced 2x2 | Nickel Even Quarters, base four | Four-man rush first | A qualified Replace |
| 11 personnel, 3x1 | Nickel Even Cover 6, passing strength | Quarters toward the passing strength, half-field opposite | The exchange rules on motion |
| Empty | Quarters or Cover 6, base four | Current matching personnel | Dime only when we can substitute |
| Bunch, stack or motion |  | Count eligibles, reset the passing strength, confirm who takes the crosser | The installed exchange rules |
| If a qualified Replace is clear against 11 personnel 2x2 | Nickel Even Quarters, Replace | Its protection target, hot coverage and run fit are clear | Base four |
| When second and long is a true pass picture | Dime Quarters or Cover 6 | Pittsburgh's personnel and support favor the pass | Nickel's run fit otherwise |
| If a four-man Replace qualifies on third and medium | Nickel Quarters or Cover 1 Robber, Replace | Choose from the release leverage | Base four |
| Counter on third and medium after a protection opportunity | Nickel Fire 3, Fire Zone | The installed real five-man counter | Only after the hot throw is identified |
| If the Thursday checks pass on third and long | Dime Quarters or Cover 6, Replace Field | Field Replace after the checks | Base four |
| If the Thursday checks pass on third and long to the boundary | Dime Quarters or Cover 6, Replace Boundary | Boundary Replace after the checks | Base four |
| When we can substitute against empty | Dime Quarters or Cover 6 | Only when the defense can legally substitute and communicate it | Current personnel |
| When we test their five-man count against empty | Interior mug | Not proof of a free rusher | Four rush |
| When near the goal line |  | The prepared heavy answer, not pass-first Dime on a short run surface | The base group |
| When a late lead faces a pass picture | Dime Quarters or Cover 6 | Dime against an actual pass picture | Nickel when the run is available |
| When the run remains available late | Nickel Quarters or Cover 6 | Nickel's run fit | Dime against a pass picture |
| If contain and hot coverage allow it late | Quarters or Cover 6, Replace | Replacement pressure is conditional | Four rush |
| When tempo keeps Nickel on the field | Nickel Even Quarters | The simplest call with Nickel out | Cover 3 Match |
| When tempo keeps the base group on | Under Quarters | The simplest call with the base group | Cover 3 Match |
| When tempo keeps Dime on | Dime Quarters | The simplest Dime call | Cover 3 Match |
| If the match exchange fails | Cover 3 Match | The practiced emergency simplification | Back to the match rules |

**Individual matchups / roles changed:** No change
